summary: Kingston, NH steel tower erected in January 1929 by the NH Forestry Department; manned in 1939; listed as gone; old footings remain on the summit.

facts.status_note: firelookout.org lists the tower as gone; NH Family Hikes says old fire tower footings can still be seen on the summit

access.note: Hiking trail from a part of Rockrimmon Road that ordinary vehicles can no longer use; about half a mile of walking to the trailhead; the left fork at the road end is a private driveway

visit.trail_note: Walk about half a mile down Rockrimmon Road to the trailhead; a short trail with orange blazes leads to an old fire tower access road and the summit

events.note: January 1929: new steel lookout tower and watchman's cabin erected by the NH Forestry Department on the summit, to cover towns in south central Rockingham County
March 1938: road to the tower being repaired as a WPA project; ledge and rock removed by dynamite
April 1939: Arthur P. Tucker, superintendent of Great Pond State Park, named as the lookout man at the Rock Rimmon tower (Portsmouth Herald)

corrections.why: The agency field holds a date fragment from the source's January 1929 entry. The same entry names the New Hampshire Forestry Department as the agency that erected the tower.

notes_for_editor: The date the tower came down is not in any source read, so no removal event is recorded. Not cited because the source could not be read: a Fosters.com 2017 feature (403 on fetch; search snippet only) says towns around Rock Rimmon were allowed to man the tower on a volunteer basis, and that in 1984 the towers operated on a limited basis; this needs checking before any staffing sentence is added. The NH state PDF forest-lookout-towers-history.pdf returned 403. Access is judged public from the NH Family Hikes trail description; no landowner or state statement was read, so verify before publishing the access level.
